multipleChoice.question: What time of day does Chapter 4 begin?
multipleChoice.explanation: The story opens with 'Now it is early morning' — the moon no longer shines and the sun rises.

multipleChoice.question: Where does the farmer go first thing in the morning to wash his body?
multipleChoice.explanation: The farmer wants to wash his body, so he goes out and travels toward the river, where the water is good.

multipleChoice.question: What is the farmer's name?
multipleChoice.explanation: The story reveals that the name of the farmer is Jacob.

multipleChoice.question: Where does Jacob live?
multipleChoice.explanation: Jacob is a Galilean and dwells in Galilee.

multipleChoice.question: What is the name of Jacob's friend?
multipleChoice.explanation: The name of Jacob's friend is Philip.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Jacob decide not to work in the field today?
options: He wants to go to the village to see his house and family
He has no more work to do
multipleChoice.explanation: Jacob wants to go to the village to see his house, his wife Martha, and his children.

multipleChoice.question: What does Philip offer to do for Jacob?
options: Travel to the village with Jacob
Guard Jacob's field and animals while Jacob is away
multipleChoice.explanation: Philip says he is able and willing to guard Jacob's field and animals, and intends to stay in the field the whole day.

multipleChoice.question: How does Jacob describe Philip in his response to Philip's offer?
multipleChoice.explanation: Jacob says 'O Philip, truly you are a good and faithful friend, and I love you.'

multipleChoice.question: Who does Jacob ask about when he arrives at Philip's?
options: Philip asks about Martha and Jacob's children
multipleChoice.explanation: Philip asks Jacob 'Is your wife Martha well? And your children?'

multipleChoice.question: Jacob says he worries about something as he prepares to leave for the village. What is it?
options: Martha and the children being alone
multipleChoice.explanation: Jacob says 'I worry about the field and the animals; I do not know what I should do.'

multipleChoice.question: When Jacob departs from Philip, where does he first go?
multipleChoice.explanation: Jacob departs from Philip and goes to his own field.

multipleChoice.question: Besides thanking Philip, who else does Jacob give thanks to?
multipleChoice.explanation: Jacob says 'I give thanks to you... I also give thanks to God; for God is good and faithful.'

multipleChoice.question: How does Philip send Jacob off at the end of their conversation?
options: With bread and fruit for the journey
multipleChoice.explanation: Philip says 'Greet your household. Go with joy and peace.'

multipleChoice.question: What does Jacob eat in the morning before going to Philip?
multipleChoice.explanation: After washing and returning home, Jacob takes bread and fruit and eats.

multipleChoice.question: How does Philip respond to Jacob's thanks?
options: He also rejoices because Jacob can go to the village
He says Jacob does not need to thank him
He asks Jacob to return quickly
multipleChoice.explanation: Philip says 'And I also rejoice because you are able to go to the village.'

trueFalse.statement: At the start of Chapter 4, the moon is still shining in the sky.
trueFalse.explanation: The moon no longer shines; it is early morning and the sun rises in the sky.

trueFalse.statement: When the farmer wakes up, he is still weary from the previous day.
trueFalse.explanation: The farmer is no longer weary but is strong when he wakes from sleep.

trueFalse.statement: The farmer has fear in his heart when he wakes up.
trueFalse.explanation: He has no fear but has peace in his heart.

trueFalse.statement: Jacob goes to the river because the water there is good.
trueFalse.explanation: The story says the water of the river is good, and Jacob washes his body there.

trueFalse.statement: Jacob is not working in the field today because he wants to visit the village.
trueFalse.explanation: Today Jacob does not work in the field but goes toward the village to see his house and family.

trueFalse.statement: Philip lives far away from Jacob.
trueFalse.explanation: Philip is near Jacob, which is why Jacob goes to him first.

trueFalse.statement: Philip has a large field and many animals.
trueFalse.explanation: Philip has a large field and many animals in the field.
Jacob's wife's name is Martha, as Philip asks about her: 'Is your wife Martha well?'

trueFalse.statement: Jacob tells Philip that his wife and children are not well.
trueFalse.explanation: Jacob says 'Yes, all are well' when Philip asks about Martha and the children.

trueFalse.statement: Jacob has been staying in the field for a long time before this visit.
trueFalse.explanation: Jacob says 'For already I have stayed in the field a long time.'

trueFalse.statement: Philip says he cannot help Jacob because he has his own work to do.
trueFalse.explanation: Philip says he is able to help Jacob and wants to guard Jacob's field and animals.

trueFalse.statement: Jacob and Philip are both farmers.
trueFalse.explanation: The story says 'They are both farmers' after describing both men's fields.

trueFalse.statement: Jacob greets Philip again with 'Peace to you, O friend' before departing.
trueFalse.explanation: Jacob greets Philip again saying 'Peace to you, O friend' before departing.

trueFalse.statement: When Jacob arrives at Philip's house, Philip does not know why he has come.
trueFalse.explanation: Philip asks 'Why do you come here early, O friend?' — he does not yet know Jacob's reason.

trueFalse.statement: Jacob gives thanks to God as well as to Philip.
trueFalse.explanation: Jacob says 'I give thanks to you... I also give thanks to God; for God is good and faithful.'

yesNo.question: Does the farmer wake up feeling strong on the morning of Chapter 4?
yesNo.explanation: He is no longer weary but strong, and has peace in his heart, not fear.

yesNo.question: Does Jacob work in the field on the day of this story?
yesNo.explanation: Today Jacob does not work in the field; he goes toward the village instead.

yesNo.question: Is Philip Jacob's neighbor and fellow farmer?
yesNo.explanation: Philip is near Jacob and has a large field; they are both farmers.

yesNo.question: Does Jacob know who will guard the field before he goes to Philip?
yesNo.explanation: Jacob wonders 'who will guard the field and the animals?' and goes to Philip first.

yesNo.question: Does Philip agree to guard Jacob's field and animals?
yesNo.explanation: Philip says he is able and willing to guard Jacob's field and animals and will stay the whole day.

yesNo.question: Does Jacob love his house?
yesNo.explanation: Jacob says 'I love my house' more than once in the conversation with Philip.

yesNo.question: Is Philip's house located in the village?
yesNo.explanation: Jacob's house is in the village; Philip's house is not mentioned — Philip is near Jacob's field.

yesNo.question: Does Jacob depart from Philip with joy and peace?
yesNo.explanation: Philip sends Jacob off saying 'Go with joy and peace,' and Jacob departs after greeting Philip again.

yesNo.question: Does Jacob say that God is good and faithful?
yesNo.explanation: Jacob gives thanks to God and says 'for God is good and faithful.'

yesNo.question: Does Jacob worry about his family while he is away?
yesNo.explanation: Jacob worries about the field and animals, not his family — he says all his family are well.

yesNo.question: When Jacob greets Philip, does he embrace him?
yesNo.explanation: Jacob comes to Philip, greets him, and Philip embraces his friend.
